transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this video. In the next few minutes, I'll show you how to log in, find your referral link, and secure your Bellver account with 2FA, two-factor authentication. Let's get started.
Open your welcome email and tap Open Your Dashboard. You can also go straight to app.bellvercards.com. Enter your username, then your password, and tap Login. Close the news window.
This is your dashboard. Your username sits at the top. Right below it is your referral link. If you plan to share BellverCard, tap the copy icon to copy it. Sharing is always optional.
Now scroll down the menu and open Settings. Check that your email shows Verified, and that your username is correct.
To update your name or mobile number, tap Edit Profile. Your email can't be changed here. Make your changes and tap Save.

Now the most important step. Under Authenticator app, tap Set Up. Open Google Authenticator on your phone and scan the QR code. If you can't scan it, type in the setup key instead. Never share this code or key with anyone. Enter the six digit code the app shows, and tap Turn On.

Save these recovery codes now. They're your only way back in if you lose your phone. Each code works once, and this is the only time they're shown. Tap Copy All, and keep them somewhere safe, offline.

A passkey lets you sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. It only works on bellvercards.com, so a fake site can't trick it out of you. Next, tap Set Code Now. Your security code is six digits, and it opens My Wallet and My Cards. Keep it safe and never forget it. Enter it, tap Continue, enter it again, and tap Set Security Code.
You can also change your password here at any time.

Now let's test it. Open your profile menu and tap Log Out. Log in again with your username and password. Bellver now asks for a code. Open Google Authenticator, type the six digit code, and tap Confirm.
You're in. Your account is now protected with two-factor authentication.

transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this video. In the next few minutes, I'll show you how to open your Web3 wallet inside your Bellver dashboard, and how to export and back up your private key, safely. Let's get started.
Go to app.bellvercards.com. Enter your username, then your password, and tap Login.
If you see "These credentials do not match our records", don't panic. Check your username and password carefully, type them again, and tap Login.
Your account is protected with two-factor authentication, so Bellver asks for a code. Open Google Authenticator, type the six digit code, and tap Confirm. Close the news window.
In the menu, tap My Wallet. Enter the six digit security code you set up in the previous video. It unlocks automatically.

This is My Wallet. There's a short two minute video here about your wallet password and private key. Watch it when you have time. Now scroll down. Here is your wallet, with BNB Chain selected by default. BNB Chain is the network we'll use to fund your wallet in the next video.
Scroll down a little, and tap Settings.

Stop, and read this warning carefully. If you lose or forget your private key or password, you lose everything. Your balance, and your position in the matrix, no matter how many team members you've already built. Bellver has no control over your wallet, and can never fix it for you. You alone are responsible.
Under General, tap Account and Security. Here you can set a wallet password. Today, we export the private key. Tap Export Private Key.

Read this screen. Your wallet is ready. Back up your key to protect your assets. This is a non-custodial wallet, so you are always in control. Keep your key private. It controls your account and your assets. Tick the box: I am responsible for safeguarding and using my wallet key information. Then tap Reveal.

This is your private key. In this video it stays hidden, and yours should too. Anyone who has this key can empty your wallet. Highlight the whole key carefully, from the very first character to the very last, and copy it.

Now back it up, offline. Write it down on paper, check every character twice, and keep it somewhere safe. Never save it in a screenshot, an email, cloud notes, or WhatsApp. And never share it with anyone. Not a friend. Not a business partner. Not even Bellver support. No one. It's called a private key for a reason. Then tap I'm Done.
Tap Dashboard to go back. When you're finished, always log out. Open your profile menu, and tap Log Out. It keeps your account safe.

Quick recap. In this video, we logged in with two-factor authentication. We opened My Wallet with the security code. We read the warning. We exported the private key, backed it up on paper, and logged out.

Well done. You now hold the key to your own wallet, and you know how to protect it. Now it's your turn, and it takes less than five minutes. transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this training. The first question almost everyone asks me about the Bellver Card is a good one. Where does my money actually sit? And is it safe? In the next few minutes, I'll show you exactly where your money lives, who holds the key, and how it moves from your wallet to your card. Let's get started.

Here's the big picture. Your money lives in two places. Place one: your Dynamic Wallet. Place two: your card. Think of your home. You keep your savings in a safe at home, and you only carry what you need for the week in your pocket. Your Dynamic Wallet is the safe. Your card is your pocket.

Let's open the safe. When you register, Bellver automatically creates a Dynamic Wallet for you. It runs on Fireblocks wallet technology. And it's non-custodial. That means the wallet belongs to you, not to Bellver. Bellver says it cannot freeze your wallet, and cannot touch your funds.

So what opens the safe? Your private key. Only you hold it. You can export it any time, and move your funds to another wallet if you ever want to. But here's where the safe example stops. A real safe has a locksmith. Your wallet does not. There's no bank to call if you lose your private key. So write it down, keep it offline, and never share it. Not with support, not with me, not with anyone. Then add a transaction password, and two-factor authentication, or a passkey. Tutorials 2 and 3 show you exactly how.

What goes into the safe? Stablecoins: USDT or USDC. A stablecoin is designed to stay worth about 1 US dollar, so your balance doesn't jump up and down like Bitcoin. Send them from any exchange or wallet. BNB Smart Chain is the recommended network, because it's cheap. Tron and Ethereum work too. Already hold Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana? Deposit them, then swap to USDT or USDC inside your wallet. No crypto yet? Open an exchange account, like VALR in South Africa, or Binance in most other countries. And keep about $10 of BNB in your wallet, for network fees.

Now your pocket: the card. Your card is a US dollar card account. You can pay in shops and online, anywhere in the world, in the local currency. Money only reaches your card when you move it there. That's called a top-up. Each top-up has a 3.9% fee, added on top. Load $100, and $103.90 leaves your wallet. The minimum top-up is $10. Once money is on your card, it sits in your card account, with Bellver's card provider. So move only what you plan to spend, just like taking cash out of the safe for the week. Everything else stays in your wallet, under your own key.

So who's behind all this? Bellver Markets Limited, based in Malta, runs the program and the rewards. Bellver describes itself as the marketing company. It does not hold your money. The card is registered in Singapore, one of Asia's leading financial centres. At the launch webinar, Bellver's head of operations in Singapore said the card provider is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and that the wallets run on Fireblocks. The platform launched as version 1.0 in September 2026, and improvements are still rolling out. Don't just trust me. Check the official documents and the launch webinar on my guide, then decide for yourself.

Let's put it all together. Your exchange sends USDT, on BNB Smart Chain, to your Dynamic Wallet. Your safe, your key. When you want to spend, you top up your card. Then you pay, with your card, your phone, or a ring.

Quick recap. Your money lives in two places: your wallet, and your card. Your wallet is yours alone, and only you hold the key. Fund it with USDT or USDC on BNB Smart Chain. Move to your card only what you plan to spend. And protect your private key like the keys to your house.

Well done. Now you know exactly where your money sits, and that puts you ahead of most people who ask. It's your turn. Open your dashboard, find your Dynamic Wallet, and check that your private key is backed up safely. And once you understand it, explain it to someone else. That's how we learn best. If you still have questions after watching this, contact me, or the business partner who shared this video with you.

Quick reminder: none of this is financial advice. Always do your own research. Thank you for watching, and for every like, share and comment. This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Wealth for the rest of us.

transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this training. Basic, Premium, Business or Gold? Physical or virtual? And what is the Special Edition? In the next few minutes, I'll help you choose the right Bellver Card for you, without guessing. Let's get started.

First, the good news. All four levels are the same card, with the same app and the same wallet behind it. You pay once, when you buy it. Bellver's price list shows no monthly or annual card fee. Only three things change between the levels: how much you can spend, how deep your rewards can go, and the price.

Let's start with spending. Think of a shopping trolley. A bigger trolley carries more. Basic lets you spend $1,000 a day, and $500 in one payment. Premium: $10,000 a day, $5,000 per payment. Business: $50,000 a day, $10,000 per payment. And Gold: $250,000 a day, and $20,000 in one payment. So ask yourself: what is the biggest payment I will ever make in one go? Choose a trolley that fits it.

Now, rewards. Think of a lift in a tall building. Your card decides how high the lift can go. Basic has no lift. It earns direct commissions only, when people order through your link. Premium can go up to level 12. Business up to level 15. And Gold up to level 20. Your stars decide how many of those floors you have unlocked. And to be paid each month, you load at least $100 onto your own card that month. That is not a subscription, and it is not a fee. It is your own money, on your own card, ready for you to spend.

So which one is for you? If you just want a good card, Basic, at $99, does the job. If you want monthly rewards, Premium, at $270, is the minimum Bellver recommends. Business, at $490, is the most popular choice. Refer 3 people who also choose Business, and the $200 commissions cover your card, with $110 to spare. Gold, at $990, gives you the highest limits and the deepest rewards. Not sure yet? Start where you are comfortable. You can upgrade later and pay only the difference. Basic to Business costs $391, and you keep the same card. Just remember: rewards are not back-dated. What you could have earned before upgrading is not paid later.

Next: physical or virtual? Both carry the same limits and the same rewards. The virtual card is a Mastercard. It's ready as soon as it's issued, there's no shipping, and you can add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay, or an NFC ring, and pay with a tap. The physical card is a Visa. It works for cash at ATMs, with a 2% fee. Shipping is $85 to Europe, or $149 to the rest of the world, and Bellver's terms allow up to 4 weeks for delivery. When you order one, give a complete shipping address, and a valid mobile number from the country where it will be delivered. Without them, the courier can't deliver your card.

Two optional extras. The Special Edition is Bellver's privacy-first version of any level. It costs $370 when you buy your card, or $470 if you upgrade later, so decide at the start. And for $49, you can have your name printed on your card.
And the usage fees, the same on every level: 3.9% when you top up, added on top. 1.75% per payment. And 2% at an ATM.

Quick recap. Same card, four sizes. Bigger levels mean bigger limits and deeper rewards. Want rewards? Start at Premium. Want to start paying today? Go virtual. Need cash from ATMs? Add a physical card. And you can always upgrade later, paying only the difference.

Well done. Now you can choose your card with confidence. It's your turn. Open the Payback Calculator on my guide, pick a level, and see how many referrals would cover it. And once you've chosen, help someone else choose theirs. If you still have questions after watching this, contact me, or the business partner who shared this video with you.

Quick reminder: none of this is financial advice. Always do your own research. Thank you for watching, and for every like, share and comment. This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Wealth for the rest of us.

transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this training. In the next few minutes, I'll show you how to fund your Bellver wallet with BNB and USDT, and how to order your first card, step by step. Let's get started.

Before you start, have four things ready. One: a little BNB, about $10 worth, for network fees. Two: USDT for your card, plus $10 extra. For Premium, that's $280. Three: your ID, for the identity check. Four: your security code and wallet password.
Why BNB first? Every transfer on BNB Chain pays a small network fee, and that fee is paid in BNB. Without a little BNB in your wallet, your USDT can't move, and your card payment can't go through.

On your dashboard, tap Deposit. This is your embedded wallet. Stay on Receive. Read the red message: only send USDT or USDC, on BNB Chain or Tron. BNB Chain is already selected. Read this warning too: only send USDT or USDC, BEP-20, on BNB Chain, plus a little BNB for network fees. Anything else, or the wrong network, means permanent loss.
Network fee covered means the BNB in this wallet pays your network fees. Scroll down to your wallet address. Scan the QR code with your phone, or tap Copy Wallet Address.

Now open the wallet or exchange you send from. This training uses Binance, but any wallet you know well works. Tap Withdraw, and choose BNB. Paste your Bellver address. Now the most important part: the network. Choose BSC, BNB Smart Chain, BEP-20. Read this: make sure the address supports BNB Smart Chain, or your assets could be lost.
Enter your amount, or tap Max. Sending to a new address for the first time? Send a small test amount first. Tap Withdraw.
Confirm the network. Who are you sending to? Yourself. Tap Next. It's a self-hosted wallet, your own Web3 wallet. Tick the declaration, and tap Submit.
Check the address and the network one last time. Crypto transactions can't be cancelled. Tap Continue.
Complete Binance's security checks. No passkey? Choose another method, then enter your authenticator code and your email code.
Sent. Back in Bellver, if you were logged out while you were away, just log in again. And there it is: gas received. This BNB pays your network fees on BNB Chain. Tap Awesome.
Part two: USDT, to pay for your card. Tap Deposit again, check BNB Chain, and copy your address.

First, decide which card you want. Premium is $270, with $10,000 a day. If you can, look at Business, Bellver's most popular card, or Gold, for higher limits. This training uses Premium, on a training account.

In Binance, withdraw USDT to the same address, on BSC again. Send your card price plus $10. In this training, 271 was typed. Don't repeat that: for Premium, send $280. Confirm, submit, and verify, just like before.
Deposit received. Tap Awesome.
Now open My Cards, and enter your security code. No cards yet. Want to take part in the 2x2 matrix? You'll need at least Premium. The matrix is optional.
Tap Order a Card. Choose your package. Prices differ because of the daily, monthly and per transaction limits, and matrix access. Choose Premium.

A virtual card is a Mastercard, issued instantly, for online payments, Apple Pay and Google Pay. A physical card is a Visa, with an $85 postage fee, and it can take up to four weeks. In this training, we order the virtual card.

The regular card needs a completed identity check. Tap Start Your Check, fill in your details, and upload your ID. The ID in this training stays hidden. Then wait until your identity is verified. If your ID has no expiry date, ask Bellver support before you submit. Bellver emails you once you're verified, and verified members skip the surcharge on cards ordered without a check.
Back to Premium, Virtual, Regular. You're verified. Nothing to add. Tap Continue.
Give your card a nickname, pick a colour, and tap Save and Continue.
Features and fees. Issuance: $270. Minimum fund: $10. $10,000 a day, $5,000 per transaction, and $20,000 a month. Tap Accept and Continue to Payment.

Here's a surprise that catches many people out. Your card starts with an opening balance of at least $10. $10 plus $270: the total is $280. In this training, $10 more had to be added. Add it from the start, and you won't get stuck here. Tick both boxes, and tap Pay.
Enter your wallet password, and tap Unlock and Pay. Wait for the network to confirm. Your card is issued! Tap View My Cards.
Top up received: that's your $10, now on your card. Tap Awesome. From here you can top up, freeze your card if anything feels wrong, and add it to a digital wallet.

This phone is an Android, so we choose Google Pay. Follow the six steps. Open Google Wallet, tap Add to Wallet, and choose New Credit or Debit Card. There's nothing to scan, so enter your details manually. Tap Reveal Card Number, and type the number, the expiry month and year, and the CVV. Never share these. Accept the terms, and enter the verification code. In this training, it came by email. Ready to pay contactless!
Back on the dashboard, the wallet is almost empty. Everything went to the card. And this Premium account now qualifies for 10 levels.

Quick recap. In this video, we prepared what you need. We funded the wallet with BNB for network fees. We added USDT for the card. We completed the identity check. We ordered a virtual Premium card, and added it to Google Pay.

Well done. You just ordered your Bellver Card, step by step. Now it's your turn. Get your BNB, your USDT plus $10, and your ID ready, and it goes smoothly. transcript: This is Dr RaShon, Your Digital Architect. Thank you for taking the time to watch this training. As promised, this is the full walkthrough of your Bellver dashboard. In the next few minutes, I'll show you where everything is, what every number means, and where to find the official company channels and documents. Let's get started.
To log in, go to app dot bellvercards dot com, forward slash login, or tap any Login button, like the one on my guide. When you log in, Dashboard is already selected.
At the top, you see the username you registered with. Next to it is the eye icon. Tap it to hide or show your balances across the dashboard. Tap it again to show them.

Below that is My Rank. This training account says Member. Then My Referral Link. Tap the copy icon to copy it, and share it with your potential business partners, if you decide to take part in the matrix program. Remember, the matrix program is one hundred percent optional.

On the right, Qualified for levels shows how many levels you qualify for. Here it's ten. Number of team members in total is still zero on this new account. And Team card top-ups this month in total shows what your team loaded onto their cards this month. These numbers grow with your team.

On the far right, Qualification direct members lists the people who registered directly under you. Tap See all direct members for the details. Below it, Monthly qualification shows your card spending this month. Your first month is free. After that, load at least one hundred dollars onto your own card every month. Now, please don't let this scare you. It scares many people at first. This one hundred dollars is not a monthly subscription, and it's not a fee. Bellver doesn't take it from you. It stays your own money, on your own card, ready for things you already buy, like groceries, fuel, data or your bills. It simply keeps you qualified for the monthly matrix rewards.

Now, this is important. Follow Bellver's official WhatsApp channels, so you're always updated. Tap Connect next to the English channel, and follow it. The second one is the German channel. Always follow the company's official socials, including Bellver's official YouTube channel. Can't find them? Ask me, or the business partner who shared this video with you.

Now the first block: Current balance in my Dynamic Wallet. This is the wallet you created and secured in Tutorial 3. It's provided and secured by Fireblocks, a non-custodial wallet, protected by your private key. Haven't watched Tutorial 3 yet? Watch it now. Watched it already? Watch it again, as a quick refresher.

Commissions in 24 hours: what you earned in the last twenty four hours, still clearing. Rewards current month: your rewards for the current reward period. And Missing Rewards: rewards your card level would make you miss. This one reads: your card already earns you every level your partners qualify you for. If anything ever shows here, the Deposit and Upgrade buttons are right there.

Current balance on all of my cards: the total on every card you bought from Bellver. Here it's ten dollars. Lifetime Direct Commissions in total: all your cleared commissions for your personal referrals. Lifetime Rewards in total: all the rewards you ever received. And Earnings Available: the total of your earnings available for withdrawal. All these numbers update as you build your business.

My active cards shows your cards. This one is a Premium virtual card. More cards would show here too, and you can tap Upgrade at any time. Next, Lifetime deposits in total, and Lifetime spendings in total on all your cards. This card hasn't been used yet, so it shows zero.
